claim: Consider two binary scoring rules evaluated on the same number \(N\) of cases and the same number \(P\) of positives, with all scores distinct. After sorting each rule from highest to lowest score, represent its ranking by a binary word of length \(N\), with \(1\) at positive cases. Let \(A\) be ROC area under the curve and let \(\mathrm{AP}\) be classical average precision. No pair of such rankings receives opposite strict orderings from \(A\) and \(\mathrm{AP}\) for \(N\le4\). At \(N=4\), weak-order agreement first fails only because, for \(P=2\), the rankings \(1001\) and \(0110\) both have \(A=1/2\) while their average precisions are \(3/4\) and \(7/12\). At \(N=5\), strict reversal appears for the first time, in exactly two unordered pairs across all prevalences. For \(P=2\), \(10001\) versus \(01100\) has \(A:1/2<2/3\) but \(\mathrm{AP}:7/10>7/12\). For \(P=3\), \(10011\) versus \(01110\) has \(A:1/3<1/2\) but \(\mathrm{AP}:7/10>23/36\). If the positive ranks are \(1\le r_1<\cdots<r_P\le N\) and \(Q=N-P\), then \(A=1-\sum_{j=1}^{P}(r_j-j)/(PQ)\), whereas \(\mathrm{AP}=P^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{P}j/r_j\). Thus ROC-AUC depends only on the total positive displacement below the ideal ranking, while average precision is sensitive to where that displacement occurs; the five-case witnesses are the smallest exact manifestation of that difference.
integrity: ROC-AUC is reduced exactly to total positive displacement from the ideal ranking, while average precision is an exact reciprocal-rank sum. Every binary ranking with both classes present through total five is enumerated, and every pair is compared within fixed prevalence using rational arithmetic.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns finite binary rankings with a fixed positive prevalence and no score ties. Average precision is the classical discrete mean of precisions at positive ranks; the result does not cover every interpolation convention for precision-recall area or statistical uncertainty in estimated performance.
title: Five ranked cases are the sharp ROC-AUC–average-precision strict-reversal boundary
